speaker: Doctor
text: I notice your history mentions mental status changes, but I have no record of your symptoms or medical history yet. Can you describe exactly what changes you or your family have noticed in your behavior or thinking?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old female. The patient has been brought to the emergency room by her family due to altered mental status. The family mentions that she has been increasingly confused over the past few days. No recent head trauma or known drug use. The patient has a smoking history of 30 pack-years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. To narrow down the cause of her confusion, does she have a history of liver, kidney, or thyroid disease, and has she been experiencing any nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain? Also, what are her vital signs, specifically her blood glucose level and temperature?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mental status changes. I also have Increased confusion, Lethargy.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hepatic Encephalopathy. The combination of significant smoking history, new-onset confusion, lethargy, and lack of other systemic symptoms strongly suggests liver failure. Given the high probability, I am requesting a Liver Function Test panel and an abdominal ultrasound to confirm.
